LEGO Ideas Alfa Romeo Montreal Mirrors the Best Italian Car That Launched at the Worst Possible Time
12 photos
Photo: LEGO Ideas/Musstrafaccatrator
No matter how big the passion for automobiles some people have, the majority of them would probably have a hard time trying to remember what the Alfa Romeo Montreal is. Nobody can blame them for that, of course, but this reality makes the LEGO Ideas set we have here even more surprising.
The Montreal was born as a concept car on request for the 1967 Universal Exposition held in the namesake Canadian city. Put together in just nine months, it was penned by Bertone's Marcello Gandini and used a Giulia Sprint GT as a base.
There were several things setting this streamlined coupe apart from pretty much everything else that was available at the time: a low radiator grille, headlights half-concealed by the car's hood, making them look like eyes with eyelids, the two long doors , and the almost horizontal glass at the rear.
For the purpose of the 1967 Universal Exposition, Alfa Romeo only put together two Montreals, which were proudly displayed at the main entrance and, thanks to a clever play of mirrors, repeatedly transported inside the exhibition space.
The concepts proved quite the hit among those attending, so Alfa decided to make it for the masses. That's how a production version was quickly conceived, using technologies from cars such as the 33 Stradale and a series of design changes meant to be more user-friendly, if you will.
The car would have probably been a huge hit if it weren't for the troubles that defined the early 1970s. Shown at the 1970 Geneva International Motor Show, the production Montreal started rolling off the lines two years later.
A few years after that, with just 3,925 units produced by 1977, the same production lines stopped, on account of the oil crisis and the public's interest in such cars plummeting into the abyss.
The LEGO Ideas set I stumbled upon these days tries to bring back the Montreal, this time in plastic brick form. The work of a fan designer who goes by the name Musstrafaccatrator, the set comes to life after an unspecified number of parts are properly assembled, forming a design that comes with a working steering system, opening doors, trunk and hood, and a replica of a V8 engine under the hood.
The set was submitted for public voting in the summer of last year, and it has gained 3,053 backers since that time. It only has 141 days left to get to 5,000 and get an extension before an official evaluation can be performed when double that number is reached.
Until we get to learn if the Montreal is coming back as a LEGO set or not, there's always the option to go see the two real-life prototypes in their pearl white overalls. That's because the concepts are now part of the FCA Heritage collection, displayed at the Alfa Romeo History Museum in Milan, Italy.
